title: Model Catalog Demo - Acme Health
summary: Redwood demo focused on the model catalog: how to pick open models, review benchmark numbers, and use compatibility matrices to map models to Acme Health's Dedicated and Private deployments. Customer asked about latency/cost tradeoffs, quantized variants, and SOC2/KMS compliance. Agreed to run a short POC benchmarking their sample prompts on a dedicated instance and share detailed spreadsheets and security docs.
action_items: Lily Chen - share model catalog CSV + benchmark sheet - due 2026-03-23
Marco Ruiz - prepare POC run plan and list of compatible quantized builds - due 2026-03-27
Acme (Samuel) - provide 100 sample prompts + expected latency SLOs - due 2026-03-22
next_steps: Send model catalog export and benchmark worksheet
Schedule POC kickoff (30-60 minutes) for next week
Share SOC 2 and KMS integration docs with Jorge
Follow up on pricing for Dedicated trial
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-20 15:00 PDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Lily Chen, Marco Ruiz (Redwood); Dana Patel, Samuel King, Priya Reddy, Jorge Alvarez (Acme)

[00:00] Lily Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick model catalog walkthrough, show how you can select open models, look at benchmarks, and the compatibility matrix with Dedicated and Private options.
[00:12] Dana Patel: sounds good, we've been evaluating a couple options, curious how Redwood's catalog helps us pick models that fit our latency/cost tight constraints for chart summarization.
[00:20] Marco Ruiz: great, couple quick notes - the catalog surfaces model versions, verified throughput profiles, and recommended quantization presets. we'll demo how a model like luminate-open-7b performs in fp16 vs int8. apologies, some names in the UI are truncated sometimes.
[00:35] Priya Reddy: when you say "verified throughput" what does that mean? are these your internal numbers or customer-observed?
[00:41] Marco Ruiz: a mix - we run standardized benchmarks on our infra and also annotate community reports; the catalog shows median p50/p95 latencies for typical seq lengths and cost per 1k tokens estimates. for Dedicated we include observed throughput at different batch sizes.
[00:55] Samuel King: do you have a compatibility matrix to tell us which quant builds are supported on our Dedicated GPU types? we're running A10s and some T4s in our staging.
[01:05] Marco Ruiz: yes, the compatibility matrix maps models -> variant (fp16, int8, int4) -> recommended kernel path -> supported hardware. for example the luminate-open-7b-int8 is supported on A10 and RTX6000, but int4 is alpha on T4s and may hit higher error rates.
[01:20] Jorge Alvarez: security - if we roll Private, can the control plane still reference the model catalog? we need to keep model metadata locally and ensure KMS never leaves our VPC.
[01:28] Lily Chen: good q. Private supports a local model-catalog mirror; metadata lives in your control plane and outbound calls for telemetry are opt-in. KMS integrations (HSM/KMS) are supported - we'll share the integration matrix.
[01:40] Dana Patel: benchmarks - i'd like to see p95 numbers for 512 token summaries and cost per 1k tokens on both Hosted and Dedicated. last time we saw int8 gave ~2x cost savings but throughput variance was tricky.
[01:52] Marco Ruiz: exactly - int8 often reduces GPU memory and token cost but can increase variance and sometimes degrades qa for certain prompts. the catalog includes PROMPT-SPECIFIC evals (we call them eval sets) so you can filter benchmarks by prompt type - seq length distribution and task (summarization vs QA).
[02:08] Priya Reddy: can you show the UI?
[02:12] Marco Ruiz: sure, screen share now. (screen share) ok, top-left is the model catalog list - filter by architecture, size, and tags: "num_params", "medical_finetuned", "open-source". clicking luminate-open-7b brings up a panel with: supported_variants, performance_profile, accuracy_scores, and a link to community notes.
[02:30] Marco Ruiz: here you can toggle variant: fp16 baseline, int8 quantized, and our optimized kernel path. see bench table: p50 45ms, p95 120ms for 1-token warm short prompt on A10 in Dedicated at batch=1; for 512 tokens p95 ~1.1s - again this is median across runs, your workload can differ.
[02:50] Samuel King: those numbers are promising. what about latency under sustained throughput? we care about tail during bursts.
[02:57] Marco Ruiz: the catalog includes throughput curves and tail latency plots. there's also a recommended autoscale config which balances cost and tail. worth noting we do prefix and KV cache recommendations: frequently used system prompts can be cached which reduces hot path latency. sometimes the transcription says "KV cash" in older logs, but it's KV cache.
[03:15] Dana Patel: how are regressions handled if we switch model versions? we need automated quality checks.
[03:21] Lily Chen: Redwood Optimize ties model/version rollouts to eval sets. you can define a baseline prompt set and set thresholds - if a new rollout degrades closed-book accuracy or hallucination metrics, the rollout can auto-failover. we'll show a quick example in the console.
[03:36] Priya Reddy: about the compatibility matrix - can we export it? our infra team wants a CSV mapping to our GPU SKUs.
[03:41] Marco Ruiz: yes, exportable CSV and a REST endpoint. we'll include supported kernels and notes on memory footprint.
[03:50] Jorge Alvarez: SSO and audit - does model selection actions get logged? we need audit logs for who changed model pinning.
[03:56] Lily Chen: yes, RBAC + audit logs track model pinning, rollouts, who triggered POCs. SOC 2 and ISO artifacts available; Jorge, we'll send those docs.
[04:08] Dana Patel: one more on pricing - what does Dedicated trial look like? we'd likely want a 2-week trial with a small reserved pool to run our prompts.
[04:16] Lily Chen: we can provision a small Dedicated slice, run your sample prompts, and share cost reports token-level. pricing during trial is discounted; we'll provide a formal quote after we define capacity.
[04:25] Samuel King: for the POC can you run our 100 sample prompts? we'd like p50/p95 for each model variant and a recommended config.
[04:31] Marco Ruiz: yes, provide the prompts, and we'll schedule the benchmark run. we'll include per-prompt latency and quality deltas vs your baseline.
[04:38] Priya Reddy: any gotchas with medical content? we need data residency and encrypted logging.
[04:44] Lily Chen: for regulated data we recommend Private or VPC Dedicated; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and we can disable telemetry. KMS integration ensures keys stay on your side.
[04:54] Dana Patel: ok good. final recap?
[04:58] Lily Chen: recap - we'll share: (1) model catalog export + benchmark sheet, (2) SOC2/KMS integration docs, (3) POC run plan and quote. Acme will send 100 sample prompts and target SLOs. we'll schedule a 30m POC kickoff next week.
[05:15] Jorge Alvarez: thanks, that's all from security.
[05:18] Samuel King: thanks everyone.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-hears: e.g., "int eight" vs "int8", "KV cash" for KV cache, "S-O-C two" for SOC2. There were a few cross-talks during the screen share.
questions: Which quantized variants are supported on A10 vs T4?
Can the model catalog be mirrored to Private with local metadata?
Will Redwood run per-prompt p95/p50 for our 100 sample prompts?
